programme.sub-title: Peggy Sue: Tales of Rock and Roll
programme.desc: An interview with the woman who inspired one of Buddy Holly's most famous songs. Arena takes Peggy Sue Gerron Rackham back to Lubbock in Texas. This is where she went to the same high school as Holly and where her marriage to his drummer Jerry Allison inspired a second tribute, Peggy Sue Got Married. She reveals how both songs came to be written and provides insight into the singer's short career

programme.title: It's Only Rock 'n' Roll: Rock 'n' Roll at the BBC
programme.desc: A compilation of classic rock 'n' roll artists and songs in celebration of the musical genre. Including performances by Jerry Lee Lewis, Dion, Dick Dale and Neil Sedaka, who all featured in the Rock 'n' Roll America series. Plus, a selection of songs with rock 'n' roll in the title, such as Tom Petty's Anything That's Rock 'n' Roll, Joan Jett's I love Rock 'n' Roll and Oasis's Rock 'n' Roll Star

programme.title: Elizabeth Taylor: A Tribute
programme.desc: A programme dedicated to the Oscar-winning actress, with friends, family and co-stars sharing their memories and looking back on her career, as well as her humanitarian work and much-publicised personal life. Featuring contributions from Liza Minnelli, Joan Collins, Pierce Brosnan, Angela Lansbury, David Frost, Larry King, Robert Hardy, Barry Norman and Richard Burton's nephew Guy Masterson

programme.title: The Hunt for Lady Olive and the German Submarine
programme.desc: On the morning of February 19, 1917, German U-boat UC-18 opened fire on Royal Navy Q-ship the Lady Olive, but as the submarine drew near to assess the damage it had inflicted, the Lady Olive counter-attacked. Both vessels were said to have sunk. For decades, divers and historians have searched to discover their fate and understand the story that led to this encounter. This documentary follows film-maker Karl Taylor and his specialist team over four years as they search to uncover what happened on that fateful day in 1917

programme.title: Villages by the Sea
programme.desc: Archaeologist Ben Robinson travels to Johnshaven, a once important Scottish fishing village. When its skilled sailors were pressganged into the Royal Navy in the late 18th century, it had to diversify into the flax and jute trade - which fed into the jute capital, the nearby city of Dundee. Ben discovers the ruins of an old cloth mill used to make cloth for sails and later coarse linen sacking, a product vital for transporting goods and tries to solve the village mystery of what a circular building in a local's garden could have been

programme.title: BBC Proms

Britten's The Young Person's Guide to the Orchestra and Dvorák's 'New World' Symphony complete a the programme. Georgia Mann presents. Britten: The Young Person's Guide to the Orchestra 18'. Gwilym Simcock: Triple Concerto for Soprano Saxophone, Horn and Cello 20' BBC co-commission (world premiere). Interval. Dvorák Symphony No 9 in E minor, 'From the New World' 40'. Jess Gillam (saxophone), Ben Goldscheider (horn), Sheku Kanneh-Mason (cello), BBC Symphony Orchestra, conductor Sakari Oramo

programme.desc: Part two of two. The naturalist reaches the peak of one of Venezuela's tepui mountains, before joining a party of Italian cavers as they venture into the unexplored caverns within. Inside, they discover strange wildlife and evidence of the geological forces that give the tepuis their unusual shape. Finally, the team returns to the ground by abseiling down the Angel Falls, the world's highest waterfall

programme.title: Today at the Test
programme.desc: England v Pakistan. Highlights of day four of the Third and Final Test in the series from Edgbaston in Birmingham. Coming into this series, the visitors had only won two of their last 10 Test Series, with their last coming in December 2024 when they beat England 2-1 after losing the First Test. England have fared slightly better, winning four of their previous 10 series, but had disappointing defeats against New Zealand and Australia before they took on Pakistan

programme.title: Golf: Solheim Cup Highlights

programme.title: The Fall and Rise of Reginald Perrin
programme.desc: First episode of the classic 1970s comedy, starring Leonard Rossiter as a middle-aged executive stuck in a rut and eager to learn the real meaning of life. When Reginald Perrin set out for work on Tuesday morning, he had no intention of calling his mother-in-law a hippopotamus. But he did, and from then on everything began to change. Originally broadcast in 1976

programme.title: The Fall and Rise of Reginald Perrin

programme.title: Sound Waves: The Symphony of Physics
programme.desc: Helen Czerski investigates the science behind familiar sounds as well as those humans cannot hear. At the Palace of Westminster, she teams up with scientists to carry out measurements using state-of-the-art lasers to reveal how Big Ben vibrates to create pressure waves in the air at particular frequencies. She also explores the science of the voice, inviting soprano Lesley Garrett to sing I Dreamed A Dream inside an MRI scanner to reveal how her vocal tract acts as a resonator, amplifying and shaping the sound from her larynx

programme.title: Elizabeth Taylor: A Tribute

programme.title: The Secret Rules of Modern Living: Algorithms
programme.desc: Without people noticing, modern life has been taken over. Algorithms run everything, from search engines on the internet, to satnavs and credit-card security - they even help people travel the world, find love and save lives. Here, mathematician Marcus du Sautoy demystifies this hidden world by showing some of the most essential algorithms. He reveals where these 2,000-year-old problem-solvers came from, showing how they work, what they have achieved and how they are now so advanced they can even program themselves

It tells the tale of a little mouse who takes a walk through the woods in search of a nut, only to encounter a fox, an owl and a snake who all want to eat him. To escape their clutches, the quick-witted rodent creates an imaginary monster to scare away his attackers - but it turns out to be all too real. Robbie Coltrane heads the voice cast as the Gruffalo, with James Corden as the Mouse and Rob Brydon, John Hurt and Tom Wilkinson as the predators

programme.title: The Gruffalo's Child

The Gruffalo has raised his daughter on tales of the big, bad mouse, the only creature in the forest he is frightened of. Despite her father's warnings, she sets off in search of this scary creature, along the way encountering the snake, owl and the fox. But when she still has no luck finding the evil rodent, she begins to think he does not exist after all. Robbie Coltrane, James Corden and Rob Brydon lend their voices, with Shirley Henderson as Gruffalo Jr

Later, in the morning, there's a long wait at breakfast

programme.title: Four in a Bed
programme.desc: The third visit of the week takes place at Vera's Kitchen and B&B in Lechlade, Gloucestershire, where young owners Warren Neinaber and Emily Mapson hope to impress their guests

programme.title: Four in a Bed
programme.desc: The guests check in to the Preston Hotel in Yeovil, owned by father and son Bis and Deep Oozageer. Ann and Rebecca find their room more cheap than cheerful, although an afternoon tasting the produce at a cider brandy distillery proves a massive hit

programme.title: Four in a Bed
programme.desc: The B&B owners reunite, ready to air their grievances from throughout the week. programme.title: A Place in the Sun
programme.desc: Lee Juggurnauth jets off to Portugal's Algarve to help house-hunters Audrey and Tony find the perfect holiday home. Lee lines up five properties for them to consider, all within their budget of £220,000

programme.title: A Place in the Sun
programme.desc: Sailing fans Nicole and Lee are planning to move permanently to Aude in the south of France. Jean Johansson shows the couple five properties for their maximum budget of £270,000

programme.title: A Place in the Sun

programme.title: Come Dine with Me
programme.desc: Marketing manager Stephanie Hale hosts the first party in Nottingham, where her guests are local councillor Alex Foster, beauty therapist Janice Overton, project engineer Brian Hodges and businessman Barry Dickman. programme.title: Come Dine with Me
programme.desc: Local councillor Alex Foster throws the second party in Nottingham, hoping to impress with his French menu and a spot of bell-ringing for entertainment. However, one guest likens the host's starter to cat food, while another criticises his home's tidiness

programme.title: Come Dine with Me
programme.desc: Beauty therapist Janice Overton hosts a 1970s-themed dinner party in Nottingham. The guests seem to be in the mood when they arrive suitably dressed for the occasion, but they soon begin to feel uncomfortable as one of them reveals that he is not keen on a fellow diner

programme.title: Come Dine with Me
programme.desc: Engineer Brian Hodges hosts the penultimate dinner party in Nottingham. Knowing his skills are limited, he decides to rope in his local butcher to help out in the kitchen, borrows cutlery from a pub and persuades a friend's daughters to waitress for him

programme.title: Come Dine with Me
programme.desc: Party animal Barry Dickman hosts the final dinner party in Nottingham, hoping his Greek-themed night will be enough for him to win the competition. programme.title: Four in a Bed

programme.title: Four in a Bed

programme.title: 9/11: 102 Minutes That Changed America
programme.desc: Amateur footage and audiotape recorded by people around New York, giving an insight into their experiences of the September 11 terrorist attacks on the World Trade Centre in 2001. The duration of the tragedy, from the first plane hitting the north tower to the collapse of both buildings, was 102 minutes. During that time, many of the city's residents sought to preserve images of what was taking place. Joined together into a single, seamless historical record, the end result is an intensely personal perspective on events as they unfolded

programme.title: 24 Hours in A&E

programme.title: 24 Hours in A&E

programme.sub-title: The Clue of the Savant's Thumb

She could do with some help from her old sidekick, the master of illusion Jonathan Creek - but he has moved on and shows little interest in the case. As Joey starts digging she meets the investigating officer - Gideon Pryke, a sharp-minded DI who remembers Creek from one of his previous cases. But he's not quite the man he used to be. On the high slopes of Mount Kenya, a pregnant High Casqued Chameleon must choose the right time in a daily cycle of tropical sun and frost at night to give birth. The mountains of Japan are the snowiest place on Earth, providing hostile conditions for a lone male Macaque cast out of his troop. In the remote Southern Alps of New Zealand, parrots feed on the dead, while in the Andes, flamingos thrive in high altitude volcanic lakes

programme.title: 999 Rescue Squad
programme.desc: Yorkshire's HART paramedics race to help a man who has been stabbed in the back with a screwdriver, and there's a fire in a hotel resulting in a desperate search for those inside

programme.title: The Green Planet
programme.desc: A guide to plants that thrive in human-dominated environments, including trees that grow across canyons in India, which have developed into living bridges. The programme examines the origins of growing crops and the ongoing influence on the world of wild plants, as well as efforts to preserve species, from snipers firing pesticide bullets from helicopters to fend off invasive plants to plants being painstakingly pollinated using a paintbrush

programme.title: Frozen Planet II
programme.desc: David Attenborough explores frozen regions around the world. The first episode begins in Antarctica, where Emperor Penguin chicks are abandoned by their parents as spring begins and must find their way across the treacherous sea ice to the rich waters of the Southern Ocean. In the Himalayas, the world's fluffiest cat hunts for gerbils and voles, while in the boreal forests circling North America, Europe and Asia, a Siberian tiger is on the lookout for black bears

programme.title: Frozen Planet II
programme.desc: David Attenborough narrates a glimpse of the wildlife of the Arctic Ocean, as spring begins after four months of winter darkness. Polar bears lead their cubs to hunt, beluga whales trapped by ice see the possibility of escape, harp seals teach their pups to swim, and bowhead whales come in search of food. Plus, a look at how the region is warming faster than anywhere else on Earth due to climate change
